points.place: 瑞典斯莫兰省拉什尔特
points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 卡尔·林奈于1707年5月23日出生在瑞典斯莫兰省的一个牧师家庭。父亲尼尔森是当地的路德会牧师，对植物学有浓厚兴趣，从小教导林奈认识周围的植物。这段时期，林奈展现出对自然界的强烈好奇心和敏锐观察力，经常在家庭花园中采集植物标本。父亲的植物学知识为林奈奠定了最初的生物学基础，培养了他对分类系统的初步思考。这段乡村生活经历使林奈对自然界的多样性和秩序产生了深刻理解，影响了他后来的科学思维方式。
points.descriptionEn: Carl Linnaeus was born on May 23, 1707, in Råshult, Småland, Sweden, to a family of Lutheran priests. His father Nils was a local pastor with a keen interest in botany, who taught young Carl to recognize the plants around them. During this period, Linnaeus showed a strong curiosity and keen observation skills towards nature, often collecting plant specimens in the family garden. His father's botanical knowledge laid the foundation for Linnaeus' early biological studies and cultivated his initial thoughts on classification systems. This rural life experience gave Linnaeus a deep understanding of the diversity and order of the natural world, influencing his later scientific thinking approach.

points.title: 医学启蒙
points.description: 1727年，林奈进入隆德大学医学院学习。在这里，他遇到了医学教授斯托尔，这位教授对植物学同样充满热情，并鼓励林奈深入研究植物分类学。林奈在隆德大学期间开始发展自己的分类思想，尝试将植物按照雄蕊和雌蕊的数量和排列方式进行分类。这一时期，他阅读了大量植物学著作，包括当时著名的植物学家塞里巴的著作。1728年，林奈转入乌普萨拉大学继续医学学习，但隆德大学的经历为他后来的植物学研究奠定了重要基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1727, Linnaeus enrolled at Lund University's medical school. There he met Professor Stobaeus, who shared his passion for botany and encouraged Linnaeus to delve deeper into plant taxonomy. During his time at Lund, Linnaeus began developing his own classification ideas, attempting to classify plants based on the number and arrangement of stamens and pistils. During this period, he read extensively on botanical works, including those by the renowned botanist Sébastian Vaillant. In 1728, Linnaeus transferred to Uppsala University to continue his medical studies, but his experience at Lund laid an important foundation for his later botanical research.

points.title: 拉普兰探险
points.description: 1732年，林奈获得了资助，前往瑞典北部的拉普兰地区进行科学考察。这次历时五个月的探险行程约2000公里，林奈记录了数百种植物和动物标本，以及当地萨米人的生活方式和习俗。他特别关注了拉普兰地区的药用植物，并详细记录了它们的用途。这次考察经历极大地丰富了林奈的生物学知识，使他收集了大量第一手资料。然而，由于条件艰苦，林奈的笔记和部分标本在返回途中丢失。尽管如此，这次探险成果最终整理成《拉普兰植物志》于1737年出版，成为当时重要的植物学著作。
points.descriptionEn: In 1732, Linnaeus received funding to undertake a scientific expedition to Lapland in northern Sweden. This five-month journey covered about 2,000 kilometers, during which Linnaeus documented hundreds of plant and animal specimens, as well as the lifestyle and customs of the local Sámi people. He paid special attention to medicinal plants in Lapland and recorded their uses in detail. This expedition greatly enriched Linnaeus' biological knowledge, allowing him to collect a wealth of first-hand information. However, due to harsh conditions, Linnaeus' notes and some specimens were lost on the return journey. Nevertheless, the results of this expedition were eventually compiled into 'Flora Lapponica' and published in 1737, becoming an important botanical work of the time.

points.title: 欧洲学术交流
points.description: 1735年，林奈前往荷兰继续深造，在哈勒姆与著名植物学家简·弗雷德里克·格罗诺维乌斯相遇。格罗诺维乌斯对林奈的分类系统给予了高度评价，并帮助他出版了《自然系统》第一版。这部著作首次提出了双命名法（即属名加种名的命名系统），成为现代生物分类学的基础。在荷兰期间，林奈还结识了许多欧洲顶尖科学家，包括荷兰医生阿尔德罗万德和德国博物学家乔治·艾伯哈特·鲁费尔。这些学术交流极大地扩展了林奈的视野，他的分类系统开始在欧洲科学界获得认可。1737年，林奈在莱顿大学获得医学博士学位，为他的学术生涯奠定了重要基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1735, Linnaeus traveled to the Netherlands to continue his studies, where he met the renowned botanist Jan Frederik Gronovius in Haarlem. Gronovius highly praised Linnaeus' classification system and helped him publish the first edition of 'Systema Naturae'. This work first proposed the binomial nomenclature (the naming system using genus and species names), becoming the foundation of modern biological taxonomy. During his time in the Netherlands, Linnaeus also met many top European scientists, including Dutch physician Herman Boerhaave and German naturalist Georg Eberhard Rumphius. These academic exchanges greatly expanded Linnaeus' horizons, and his classification system began to gain recognition in European scientific circles. In 1737, Linnaeus received his medical doctorate from Leiden University, laying an important foundation for his academic career.

points.title: 学术巅峰
points.description: 1741年，林奈接受乌普萨拉大学的邀请，担任医学和植物学教授，并创建了世界上第一个植物园。在乌普萨拉大学期间，林奈完善了他的分类系统，出版了多部重要著作，包括《植物种志》(1753)和《自然系统》第12版(1766-1778)。他建立了系统的植物分类方法，将植物分为纲、目、属、种，并引入了双命名法。林奈还培养了众多学生，派遣他们到世界各地收集标本，极大地丰富了欧洲的科学知识。1761年，瑞典国王阿道夫·弗雷德里克授予林奈贵族头衔，他改名为卡尔·冯·林奈。在乌普萨拉的37年间，林奈奠定了现代生物分类学的基础，对后世科学产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1741, Linnaeus accepted an invitation to Uppsala University to serve as Professor of Medicine and Botany, and established the world's first botanical garden there. During his time at Uppsala, Linnaeus refined his classification system and published several important works, including 'Species Plantarum' (1753) and the 12th edition of 'Systema Naturae' (1766-1778). He developed a systematic plant classification method, dividing plants into classes, orders, genera, and species, and introduced binomial nomenclature. Linnaeus also trained numerous students, sending them around the world to collect specimens, greatly enriching European scientific knowledge. In 1761, King Adolf Frederick of Sweden granted Linnaeus nobility, and he changed his name to Carl von Linné. During his 37 years in Uppsala, Linnaeus laid the foundation of modern biological taxonomy and had a profound impact on later science.

appraisal.zh: 林奈被公认为现代生物分类学的奠基人，其双命名法使生物研究有了统一语言，所建立的分类体系至今仍是生物分类的基础，并为达尔文的进化论提供了框架，把生物学从描述性学问推向系统科学。也有研究者指出，他的分类带有明显的人为性，过分强调物种固定而忽视变异与进化，某些标准流于武断，对人类的划分更带有种族等级倾向。尽管其理论已被后来的科学所超越，他确立的命名与分类框架仍是现代生物学的基石。
appraisal.en: Linnaeus is widely acknowledged as the founder of modern biological taxonomy: binomial nomenclature gave biology a unified language, his classification system remains the basis of taxonomy today, and it provided a framework for Darwin's theory of evolution, turning biology from a descriptive pursuit into a systematic science. Researchers also point out that his classification was markedly artificial, overemphasizing the fixity of species while neglecting variation and evolution, that some criteria were arbitrary, and that his division of humans carried racial hierarchy. Though surpassed by later science, the naming and classification framework he established remains the cornerstone of modern biology.

supporter.zh: 林奈被誉为'现代生物学分类之父'，他的双命名法彻底改变了生物学研究方式，使科学家能够用统一的语言交流。他建立的分类系统至今仍是生物分类的基础，为达尔文的进化论提供了重要框架。林奈对自然界的系统性研究方法开创了现代科学分类的先河，他的工作使生物学从描述性科学转变为系统性科学。他对植物和动物的全面收集与分类为后世研究提供了宝贵资料，体现了科学探索的严谨精神。
supporter.en: Linnaeus is hailed as the 'Father of Modern Biological Taxonomy.' His binomial nomenclature revolutionized biological research, enabling scientists to communicate using a unified language. The classification system he established remains the foundation of biological taxonomy today and provided an important framework for Darwin's theory of evolution. Linnaeus's systematic approach to studying nature pioneered modern scientific classification, transforming biology from a descriptive science into a systematic one. His comprehensive collection and classification of plants and animals provided valuable resources for future research, embodying the rigorous spirit of scientific exploration.

critic.zh: 批评者指出林奈的分类系统存在人为性和局限性，他过分强调物种的固定性，忽视了变异和进化。他的分类标准有时过于武断，如仅根据植物的生殖器官进行分类。此外，林奈对人类分类也存在种族主义倾向，将人类划分为不同等级。他的分类方法虽然实用，但在科学理论上存在缺陷。随着生物学发展，林奈的系统需要不断修正和完善，这反映了早期科学分类的局限性。
critic.en: Critics point out that Linnaeus's classification system contains artificiality and limitations. He overemphasized the fixity of species, neglecting variation and evolution. His classification criteria were sometimes arbitrary, such as classifying plants solely based on their reproductive organs. Additionally, Linnaeus's classification of humans showed racial tendencies, dividing humans into different hierarchical levels. While his classification method was practical, it had theoretical flaws in scientific terms. With the development of biology, Linnaeus's system required continuous revision and improvement, reflecting the limitations of early scientific classification.

objective.zh: 在历史学界，林奈被视为科学革命时期的关键人物，他的工作连接了中世纪的博物学与现代生物学。他的分类系统不仅是科学工具，更是一种哲学思考，反映了人类对自然秩序的追求。在流行文化中，林奈常被描绘为痴迷于分类的学者形象，他的名字成为科学严谨性的象征。尽管他的理论被后来科学发展所超越，但他建立的命名和分类框架仍然是现代生物学的基石。林奈的工作体现了科学发展的连续性，展示了人类知识如何通过不断修正而进步。
objective.en: In historical scholarship, Linnaeus is regarded as a key figure of the Scientific Revolution, whose work connected medieval natural history with modern biology. His classification system was not merely a scientific tool but also a philosophical reflection of humanity's pursuit of natural order. In popular culture, Linnaeus is often depicted as a scholar obsessed with classification, his name becoming a symbol of scientific rigor. Although his theories have been surpassed by later scientific developments, the naming and classification framework he established remains the cornerstone of modern biology. Linnaeus's work exemplifies the continuity of scientific development, showing how human knowledge progresses through continuous refinement.

self.zh: 上帝创造了植物，但林奈创造了它们的分类。
self.en: God created plants, but Linnaeus created their classification.
